Per-pair regression statistics with qtlRegressionStats

Claude Sonnet + Vincent Carey

2026-11-15

Source: vignettes/regressionStats.Rmd
regressionStats.Rmd

Overview

qtlRegressionStats() fits, for each requested SNP-gene pair, a linear model of phenotype on genotype plus all covariates stored in the tQTLExperiment’s colData:

phenotype ~ genotype + <covariates>

It exists alongside tensorQTL, not as a replacement for it: tensorQTL is the tool for mapping cis-QTLs genome-wide, while qtlRegressionStats() gives full lm() output (coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics for every covariate, not just genotype) for a targeted set of pairs, in-process in R. This is useful for follow-up on specific genes, for building the input to qtlPCABrowser(), and any time you want the whole regression table rather than tensorQTL’s genotype-only summary.

Pairs can be processed in parallel across phenotypes (or, in gene mode, across variants) via BiocParallel::bplapply().

library(tQTLExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(S4Vectors)

Example data

The small chr22 example dataset (20 genes, 100 samples) ships with the package and needs no external downloads.

exdir <- system.file("extdata", package = "tQTLExperiment")
tqe <- tQTLExperiment(
    plinkPrefix = file.path(exdir, "chr22-n100"),
    phenoFile   = file.path(exdir, "mean-pheno-n100.bed"),
    covFile     = file.path(exdir, "cov-n100-tqtl.tsv"),
    genome      = "hg38"
)
#> Extracting number of samples and rownames from chr22-n100.fam...
#> Extracting number of variants and colnames from chr22-n100.bim...
tqe
#> class: tQTLExperiment
#> features: 20  samples: 100 
#> assays( 1 ): pheno 
#> rowRanges: GRanges with 20 features
#> colData( 11 ) covariates: int, sex, age, expr_pc1 ... 
#> geno: 100 samples x 69638 variants [BEDMatrix - lazy]
#> plinkPrefix: /private/var/folders/yw/gfhgh7k565v9w83x_k764wbc0000gp/T/RtmpcbUgAS/temp_libpath2147cb89ee3/tQTLExperiment/extdata/chr22-n100 
#> use prepareTQTL() to write inputs and get CLI command
colnames(colData(tqe))
#>  [1] "int"       "sex"       "age"       "expr_pc1"  "expr_pc2"  "geno_pc1" 
#>  [7] "geno_pc2"  "geno_pc3"  "geno_pc4"  "geno_pc5"  "geno_pc6"  "fam_index"

The covariates here are a mix of a fixed effect (sex), a continuous covariate (age), and expression/genotype PCs – no factor-expanded columns, so qtlRegressionStats()’s output has one column per covariate rather than one per factor level.

Two ways to specify pairs

Explicit pairs

Supply a data frame with phenotype_id and variant_id columns naming exactly the pairs to fit.

pairs <- data.frame(
    phenotype_id = rownames(tqe)[1],
    variant_id   = mcols(tqtlVariantRanges(tqe))[["snp_id"]][1]
)
qtlRegressionStats(tqe, pairs)
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id t._Intercept_ t.genotype     t.sex  t.age
#> 1 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#>   t.expr_pc1 t.expr_pc2 t.geno_pc1 t.geno_pc2 t.geno_pc3 t.geno_pc4 t.geno_pc5
#> 1      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#>   t.geno_pc6
#> 1      0.972

Gene symbol and cis window

Alternatively, supply symbol and a window (bp) to fit every variant within that window of the gene’s start. This requires a gene_name column in rowRanges(tqe), added by addGeneSymbols().

if (requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v79", quietly = TRUE)) {
    tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)
    head(mcols(rowRanges(tqe))[, c("phenotype_id", "gene_name")])
}
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 2 columns
#>                    phenotype_id   gene_name
#>                     <character> <character>
#> ENSG00000100181 ENSG00000100181      TPTEP1
#> ENSG00000237438 ENSG00000237438       CECR7
#> ENSG00000177663 ENSG00000177663      IL17RA
#> ENSG00000069998 ENSG00000069998       CECR5
#> ENSG00000093072 ENSG00000093072       CECR1
#> ENSG00000131100 ENSG00000131100    ATP6V1E1
res_gene <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1", window = 1000000L)
dim(res_gene)
#> [1] 1864   14
head(res_gene)
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id t._Intercept_ t.genotype     t.sex  t.age

pairs and symbol are mutually exclusive – supply exactly one.

Output shape: t_only and wideFormat

Two arguments control the shape of the result:

  • t_only: TRUE (default) returns just the t-statistic (estimate / std.error) per term; FALSE also returns the estimate, standard error, raw t-statistic, and p-value.
  • wideFormat: TRUE (default) pivots to one row per pair, with one (or two, if t_only = FALSE) columns per model term; FALSE returns the long tidy form, one row per pair x term.
# long form, full statistics -- one row per pair x covariate
long <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1", t_only = FALSE, wideFormat = FALSE)
head(long)
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id        term  estimate std.error statistic
#> 1 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G (Intercept)  1.79e-02   0.00985  1.812558
#> 2 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G    genotype -2.07e-03   0.00194 -1.067511
#> 3 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G         sex -1.03e-06   0.00285 -0.000359
#> 4 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G         age -1.02e-04   0.00013 -0.785064
#> 5 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G    expr_pc1 -3.05e-03   0.00218 -1.394788
#> 6 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G    expr_pc2 -1.93e-03   0.00260 -0.742653
#>   p.value
#> 1  0.0733
#> 2  0.2887
#> 3  0.9997
#> 4  0.4345
#> 5  0.1666
#> 6  0.4597

# wide form, t-statistics only (the input qtlPCABrowser() expects)
head(qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1"))
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id t._Intercept_ t.genotype     t.sex  t.age
#> 1 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785

The wide, t_only = TRUE form is exactly what qtlPCABrowser() and collapseFactorTstats() expect as input: one row per SNP-gene pair, one <term>.t column per covariate.

Collapsing factor-expanded columns

When a covariate matrix includes a multi-level factor (e.g. batch or population), model.matrix() expands it into several dummy columns, so the wide qtlRegressionStats() output carries one t.<var><level> column per level. collapseFactorTstats() replaces each such group with a single root-mean-square summary column, which keeps a PCA on t-statistics from being dominated by however many levels a factor happens to have.

wide <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1")
names(wide)
#>  [1] "phenotype_id"  "variant_id"    "t._Intercept_" "t.genotype"   
#>  [5] "t.sex"         "t.age"         "t.expr_pc1"    "t.expr_pc2"   
#>  [9] "t.geno_pc1"    "t.geno_pc2"    "t.geno_pc3"    "t.geno_pc4"   
#> [13] "t.geno_pc5"    "t.geno_pc6"
# no factor-expanded columns in this toy covariate set, so this is a no-op
head(collapseFactorTstats(wide))
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id t._Intercept_ t.genotype     t.sex  t.age
#> 1 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#> 2 ENSG00000100181 22:16849971A-T          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#> 3 ENSG00000100181 22:16850437G-A          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#> 4 ENSG00000100181 22:16851225C-T          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#> 5 ENSG00000100181 22:16851356C-T          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#> 6 ENSG00000100181 22:16851640C-T          1.81      -1.07 -0.000359 -0.785
#>   t.expr_pc1 t.expr_pc2 t.geno_pc1 t.geno_pc2 t.geno_pc3 t.geno_pc4 t.geno_pc5
#> 1      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#> 2      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#> 3      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#> 4      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#> 5      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#> 6      -1.39     -0.743       1.17       1.02       1.11     -0.612      0.215
#>   t.geno_pc6
#> 1      0.972
#> 2      0.972
#> 3      0.972

On the MAGE chr17 dataset used in the main vignette, the covariate matrix includes factor_batch_* and population* dummy columns, and collapseFactorTstats() reduces each group to t.batch and t.population. See ?collapseFactorTstats for the pattern arguments.

Parallelization

BPPARAM is passed straight to BiocParallel::bplapply(). Pairs are grouped by phenotype: with multiple phenotypes, groups are distributed across workers; in gene-symbol mode (a single phenotype, many variants), the inner loop over variants is parallelized instead.

qtlRegressionStats(
    tqe,
    symbol  = "TPTEP1",
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(4)
)

Chromosome-naming caveat

rowRanges(tqe) built from a SummarizedExperiment typically carries UCSC-style seqnames ("chr17"), while tqtlVariantRanges(tqe) reflects the PLINK .bim convention of bare chromosome numbers ("17"). qtlRegressionStats() normalizes both by stripping any leading "chr" before comparing when symbol is used to select the cis window. If you write code that intersects rowRanges(tqe) and tqtlVariantRanges(tqe) directly, apply the same normalization:

sub("^chr", "", as.character(seqnames(gr)))
